message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that is equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.

> ⚠️ **Important note** – As of the latest Google Cloud release, the RTX A6000 is *not* one of the officially supported GPU models.  
> Google Cloud offers GPUs such as `nvidia-tesla-a100`, `nvidia-tesla-v100`, `nvidia-tesla-p100`, `nvidia-tesla-t4`, etc.  
> If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to use a custom image or a different provider that supports that GPU.  
> The example below uses the closest supported GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a100`) so that the code actually works on GCP.  
> Replace the GPU type with the one you need if it becomes available.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | How to set it up |
|------|------------------|
| **Google Cloud SDK** | Install `gcloud` from <https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install> |
| **Project ID** | Create a project in the Cloud Console or use an existing one. |
| **Billing enabled** | Ensure billing is attached to the project. |
| **API enabled** | Enable the Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`). |
| **Permissions** | You need `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (or higher) on the project. |
| **Zone** | Pick a zone that supports GPUs, e.g., `us-central1-b`. |

---

## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"          # replace with "nvidia-tesla-a6000" if available
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU + RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Attach GPU(s) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Base OS image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS) |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD for better I/O |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script that runs on first boot (e.g., install drivers) |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules |
| `--scopes` | OAuth scopes for the instance |

> **Tip:** If you need to install the NVIDIA driver automatically, add a `startup.sh` script that pulls the driver from the NVIDIA CUDA repository.

---

## 3. Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to hit the REST endpoint directly, here’s a `curl` example that uses a service account key for authentication.

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Build the JSON payload
read -r -d '' PAYLOAD <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": $GPU_COUNT,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/$GPU_TYPE"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$PAYLOAD"
```

### Explanation

- **Authentication** – Uses an OAuth 2.0 access token obtained via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`.  
- **Endpoint** – `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances`.  
- **Payload** – JSON object describing the instance.  
- **Accelerator** – The `acceleratorType` field points to the GPU type.  
- **Metadata** – The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver on boot.  

> **Note:** Replace `"nvidia-tesla-a100"` with `"nvidia-tesla-a6000"` if Google Cloud ever adds that GPU type.

---

## 4. Verifying the Instance

After creation, you can verify that the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="json(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```json
{
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 5. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **GPU type not found** | Verify the GPU type exists in the zone: `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=$ZONE`. |
| **Insufficient quota** | Request a GPU quota increase in the Cloud Console. |
| **Driver not installed** | Check the `startup-script` logs: `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output $INSTANCE_NAME`. |
| **Firewall blocking ports** | Add firewall rules: `gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-http --allow tcp:80`. |

---

## 6. Summary

- **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ...` – easiest way to spin up a GPU instance.  
- **REST**: `curl` with JSON payload – useful for automation scripts or CI/CD pipelines.  
- **GPU availability**: RTX A6000 is not currently offered by GCP; use the nearest supported GPU or a different provider.  

Feel free to copy the snippets above into your terminal or scripts, adjust the variables to match your environment, and you’ll have a GPU‑enabled Ubuntu 20.04 instance up and running in minutes!
